description: ROUND-2 VERIFICATION: RESOLVED. gates/v05.sh's real (non-FORCE) criterion-(e) arithmetic now runs a python3 `re.split(r"[.!?。！？]", text)` (lines 128-137) as the PRIMARY path -- codepoint-safe regardless of ambient locale -- and only falls back to `tr` (lines 139-149) if python3 is genuinely absent, with LC_ALL/LANG explicitly forced to a UTF-8 locale in that fallback (never an inherited ambient C/POSIX locale). A NEW dedicated discriminating test, tests/test-find002-locale-safe-sentences.sh, proves BOTH halves of the requirement: (1) a CONTROL section reproduces the OLD byte-wise `tr` splitter forced under LC_ALL=C on a genuinely-long Japanese sentence and shows it computes the WRONG verdict (crit_e=true); (2) the CURRENT gates/v05.sh, run under the SAME LC_ALL=C on the SAME fixture, computes the CORRECT verdict (crit_e=false). The red-phase evidence log (.../evidence/sprint-2-findings-fix-red-phase.log) shows this exact test FAILING against the pre-fix source, and the green-phase log shows it PASSING post-fix -- proving the fix is real and the test is discriminating, not tautological.

evidence.snippet:
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  read -r total short <<PYOUT
$(printf '%s' "$plain" | python3 -c 'import re,sys; text=sys.stdin.read(); sentences=[s.strip() for s in re.split(r"[.!?。！？]", text) if s.strip()]; print(len(sentences), sum(1 for s in sentences if len(s)<=60))')
PYOUT
else
  sentences="$(printf '%s' "$plain" | LC_ALL="${LC_ALL:-en_US.UTF-8}" LANG="${LANG:-en_US.UTF-8}" tr '.!?。！？' ...)"
